key_insight: Plasma p-tau217 is elevated in tuberous sclerosis complex and follows an age-related pattern similar to Alzheimer’s disease, suggesting shared downstream neurodegenerative biology independent of amyloid.
clinical_relevance: This biomarker could help stratify neurodegenerative risk and TAND severity in TSC and may inform future mTOR-targeted intervention studies.
method: Compared plasma p-tau217 in 63 TSC, 25 AD, and 116 cognitively unimpaired participants.
Used multivariable linear regression to test group differences in log2 p-tau217.
Applied ANCOVA to compare age-related slopes across cohorts.
evidence_signal: The study found significantly lower p-tau217 in cognitively unimpaired participants versus TSC, with no significant difference between TSC and AD, and similar age-related slopes across groups.
watch_item: The sample size was modest and cross-sectional, so longitudinal validation is needed before p-tau217 can be used as a routine prognostic tool in TSC.
paper_title: Amyloid-Independent Elevation of Plasma phosphorylated tau-217 Tracks Neurodegenerative Risk in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: Implications for mTOR-Targeted Intervention
